brief:
Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief running for prime minister, is exploring a potential power-sharing arrangement with Benjamin Netanyahu, according to Al Jazeera English. Some of his political allies have backed the idea, though such a coalition would contradict his pre-election commitment to prevent Netanyahu from returning to office.

The negotiations reflect the complex dynamics of Israeli coalition politics, where smaller parties and candidates often face pressure to compromise their stated positions to secure government positions or influence.
dek: Some of his allies are calling for such an arrangement, but it would represent a betrayal of his pre-election promise.
title: Eisenkot considers power-sharing deal with Netanyahu despite campaign pledges
